questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — ww6 (cloud chargeback platform, Next.js + Prisma). Senior-review finding F2: allocation runs store `monthStart` exactly as the caller sent it, but the chargeback report looks runs up by equality with the normalised month start, so any non-first-of-month input creates runs the report never shows. You will delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: a run created with any instant inside a month is found by the report for that month; the write path stores the normalised UTC month start instead of `new Date(monthStartIso)`.
[w3] Reuse the existing normaliser toUtcMonthWindow (as forecastService already does) rather than inventing new date math.
[w2] Scope names the second write site with the same bug: budgets are stored un-normalised despite the comment claiming normalisation.
[w2] Allowed files: allocationRunService.ts, budgetService.ts and new tests under tests/ (vitest only includes tests/**/*.test.ts).
[w3] Boundary: no Prisma schema or migration change and no backfill of existing rows in this task; the report-side equality lookup stays as it is.
[w2] Test command: `npm test` (vitest run), with the repository layer mocked so no database is needed.
[w2] Stop condition: both write sites normalised and a test proving a mid-month input is stored as the 1st 00:00Z; anything touching the run-uniqueness race (F8) is reported, not fixed.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What are the likeliest ways an agent goes wrong on this task, and what in your brief prevents each?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It normalises the READ side instead, which hides the symptom while the stored runs stay wrong for every other consumer.
[w2] It uses local-time Date math (getMonth/setDate), the exact pitfall the month helper's header warns about.
[w2] It 'fixes' F8 too by adding a unique index on (tenantId, monthStart), a schema change that would fail on existing duplicate rows.
keyPoints.quote: No uniqueness on `(tenantId, monthStart)` for runs and no in-flight check in `createRunAndQueue`

keyPoints.text: [w2] It also rewrites the queued job payload and the engine signature; unnecessary, because the engine already normalises the raw ISO itself, so the diff grows for nothing.
[w1] It tightens the request schema to reject mid-month input, changing the public API contract instead of fixing storage.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent says the fix is in and tests pass. What do you check before you accept it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] The new test fails on the original line (stores the raw instant) and passes on the fix; ask for both runs.
[w2] The budget path is fixed as well, and its comment is now true rather than deleted.
[w2] prisma/schema.prisma and the migrations are untouched in the diff.
[w2] The handback flags the rows already stored un-normalised as a follow-up data repair, since the README told callers to send the first instant.
[w1] The test output is the real vitest summary from the pinned command, not a restatement.
